answer: Timed response window. Each identity must answer a random challenge within a short pulse, and only the quickest replies reach the summit of a reward queue. Identities that miss windows accumulate decay and lose standing, a relic of past responsiveness. Enforcing this on every request means an attacker running N identities pays N times the continuous attention cost, since each must be actively monitored and answered in time; scaling beyond a few becomes infeasible without proportional labor.
